Transexual is an older term for transgender, with the intention that it would include those who hadn't started transitioning yet, and to help distinguish it as something that has nothing to do with your orientation. Nowadays, it's mostly used as a way to say that the trans person has started/finished medically transitioning or among older trans people. Some consider it a slur, I don't personally, but it's best to ask first.

"Genderqueer" is a non-binary gender. NB people are trans people who experience atypical sex dysphoria, and thus do not identify as FTM or MTF. While I believe that there is some validity to being non-binary, genderqueer is not one of the ones I support. It's typically used by gender non-conforming, non-dysphoric women who are either looking for attention, or who don't want to be one of those "nasty cishets". I blame Tumblr.

Pansexual was originally conceived as a more inclusive term to include atypical gendered/sexed people i.e. trans, intersex and non-binary. It's not really necessary, however, as bisexual already technically covers those things. It is also considered somewhat offensive by some of people, usually bisexuals themselves (since it makes it sound like they're bigots) and the trans/intersex people who don't appreciate being othered like that. Among sane thin people, pansexuality is thought of as more of a flavour of bisexuality, to more accurately describe what they're into, since not all bisexuals are into trans/intersex/NB people.
